description: The size of each funding source is measured by how many spatial records it has.

a.request: Using spatial records (`scanspatial`) matched to a project (`projects.arcregistry` = `scanspatial.arcref`), for each funding source (`projects.fundflux`, treating a missing source as its own group) compute the average ratio of bounding box Y (`boxy`) to bounding box Z (`boxz`), ignoring missing values, and the number of spatial records. Keep the funding sources whose number of spatial records is above the average of that number across all funding sources. Return one row with: the average of the kept sources' ratios; the total of their spatial record counts; and the average amount by which their counts exceed the cross-source average. No rounding.
a.sql: WITH src AS (SELECT p.fundflux, COUNT(*) AS cnt, AVG(s.boxy / NULLIF(s.boxz, 0)) AS ratio FROM scanspatial s JOIN projects p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY p.fundflux), avgc AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM src), kept AS (SELECT src.* FROM src, avgc WHERE src.cnt > avgc.avg_cnt) SELECT AVG(kept.ratio) AS avg_ratio, SUM(kept.cnt) AS total_count, AVG(kept.cnt - avgc.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess FROM kept, avgc;

c.request: Looking at spatial scan data (`scanspatial`) linked to projects (`projects.arcregistry` = `scanspatial.arcref`), which funding sources (`projects.fundflux`, treating a missing source as its own group) are bigger than average? For each funding source, work out the average ratio of bounding box Y (`boxy`) to bounding box Z (`boxz`), ignoring missing values, and how big it is. For the sources above the average size across funding sources, give one row with the average of their ratios, their combined size, and how far on average they exceed the average size. No rounding. The size of each funding source is measured by how many spatial records it has.
c.sql: WITH src AS (SELECT p.fundflux, COUNT(*) AS src_size, AVG(s.boxy / NULLIF(s.boxz, 0)) AS src_avg_ratio FROM scanspatial s JOIN projects p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY p.fundflux), avg_size AS (SELECT AVG(src_size) AS mean_size FROM src), above_avg AS (SELECT src.* FROM src CROSS JOIN avg_size WHERE src.src_size > avg_size.mean_size) SELECT AVG(above_avg.src_avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio, SUM(above_avg.src_size) AS combined_size, AVG(above_avg.src_size - avg_size.mean_size) AS avg_excess_over_mean FROM above_avg CROSS JOIN avg_size;

b.request: For each funding source (NULL `fundflux` as its own group), size = number of `scanspatial` rows joined to `projects` on `arcregistry = arcref`; average ratio = AVG(`boxy`/`boxz`) over non-null pairs; keep sources whose size exceeds the mean size across all sources, and return AVG(ratio), SUM(size), and AVG(size − mean size), unrounded
b.sql:
WITH src AS (
  SELECT p.fundflux,
         COUNT(*) AS size,
         AVG(s.boxy / NULLIF(s.boxz, 0)) AS avg_ratio
  FROM scanspatial s
  JOIN projects p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref
  GROUP BY p.fundflux
),
stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(size) AS mean_size FROM src
)
SELECT AVG(src.avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio,
       SUM(src.size) AS total_size,
       AVG(src.size - stats.mean_size) AS avg_size_diff
FROM src
CROSS JOIN stats
WHERE src.size > stats.mean_size;

d.request: Looking at spatial scan data (`scanspatial`) linked to projects (`projects.arcregistry` = `scanspatial.arcref`), which funding sources (`projects.fundflux`, treating a missing source as its own group) have more spatial records than the average across funding sources, where each source's size is its number of spatial records? For each funding source, work out the average ratio of bounding box Y (`boxy`) to bounding box Z (`boxz`), ignoring missing values. For the sources above the average size, give one row with the average of their ratios, their combined size (total spatial records), and how far on average they exceed the average size. No rounding.
d.sql: WITH src AS (SELECT p.fundflux AS fundsrc, COUNT(*) AS size, AVG(s.boxy * 1.0 / NULLIF(s.boxz, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM scanspatial s JOIN projects p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY p.fundflux), overall AS (SELECT AVG(size) AS avg_size FROM src), above AS (SELECT src.size, src.avg_ratio FROM src CROSS JOIN overall WHERE src.size > overall.avg_size) SELECT AVG(above.avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio, SUM(above.size) AS total_records, AVG(above.size - overall.avg_size) AS avg_excess FROM above CROSS JOIN overall
